claim: No early-season under bias in totals. Weeks 1-5 close under 50.05% against 50.70% for weeks 6+, pooled 1999-2025, n=6967
The totals market is close to unbiased: 50.4% under across 6967 graded regular season games since 1999
evidence: h-0001 base rate. Any totals edge must come from price or number, not from a directional lean.

claim: Move The Line quote real numbers but size them from single seasons; treat their trend claims as hypotheses to test, never as support
evidence: Their 2022 wk1-6 56-37 under figure verified exactly correct, but it is z=+1.97 on n=93 selected from 27 seasons and does not survive pooling.

claim: No incremental signal on sides. Opponent-adjusted ratings and the drive sim both land at partial correlation about -0.03 vs the close
evidence: Two independent routes: EPA ratings -0.04; drive sim -0.030 over 816 games, betting its disagreement went 46.8% ATS. Below 50, so leaning on it is actively harmful.

claim: Take the center from the market and the shape from the sim; never quote a sim spread as our number
evidence: Null test validates aggregate shape (margin sd 12.65 vs 12.75, key numbers to 2.5pp) but that is a far weaker claim than per-game accuracy, which the backtest refuted.

claim: Validate a distribution at the granularity you will use it, not in aggregate
evidence: Margin model is right unconditionally and 4.10pp wrong at half-points. Drive sim passes the null test and fails per-game. Same lesson twice.

claim: An external adversarial review finds probability bugs that my own validation passes; run one before trusting new math
evidence: Code reviewer found nb_sf non-monotone below zero, which had corrupted the very PIT test meant to catch it and fabricated a 10pp tail miss; and find_middle max() split, which flipped BUF@HOU from +0.11pp to -1.47pp.

claim: Suspect the validation when its result conveniently justifies a restriction
evidence: The tails-over-cover finding was a bug describing itself, and it gated the prop pricer to a needlessly narrow band and refused receptions outright.

claim: Player usage is projectable, player efficiency is not; shrink efficiency hard and never build a prop model on yards per target
evidence: Usage corr 0.748 vs production 0.598; yards per target corr 0.136.

claim: Preseason projections are maximally shrunk, so alpha receivers read low; the quote band is what stops that becoming a bet
evidence: Week 1 has no current-season data. A.J. Brown reads 30.7 rec yds median; a book line at 54.5 falls outside the 5-95% band and is refused rather than bet under.

claim: Market ratings and our 2025 ratings sit on the same scale (sd 0.106 vs 0.102), so the re-rate gap is real information, not compression
evidence: 15 of 32 moves negative. Largest: CIN and DAL up, ARI and MIA down, all explained by offseason our ratings cannot see.

claim: Defense is markedly less stable year over year than offense: mean 0.233 vs 0.331, and offense wins 5 of 6 paired same-metric comparisons
evidence: h-0002, 160 team-season pairs 2020+. Def EPA/play only 0.206 against off EPA/play 0.366. An independent rating should weight a defense's past far less than an offense's.

notes.note: The stability FACT survives (def 0.233 vs off 0.331, measured). Its PRESCRIPTION - that an independent rating should weight a defense's past far less - was tested directly in h-0003 and failed out of sample. The rating already discounts defense endogenously. Keep the fact, drop the prescription: the asymmetry belongs in how a re-rating is ALLOCATED across the two sides (p-0018), not in how hard each side is shrunk.

claim: Turnovers are noise year to year and must never carry weight in a forward rating: lost 0.065, forced 0.203
evidence: h-0002. Split-half is also near zero (lost 0.111, forced 0.139), so it is not even reliable within a season.

claim: Pass rate over expected (0.459) and offensive success rate (0.404) are the only team metrics that clear 0.40 year over year
evidence: h-0002. Both are style/process measures. Point margin manages only 0.384 and def EPA 0.206.

claim: Reliability caps predictiveness: def EPA has split-half 0.184, so its 0.206 year-over-year is near its ceiling and no model can fix it
evidence: h-0002. Split-half measures whether a metric measures a stable property at all; year-over-year cannot exceed it by much.

claim: Capture is now scheduled twice daily on this machine; line movement and pregame props cannot be reconstructed and are the only irreversible item before Sept 9
evidence: Two snapshots existed 78 minutes apart. Windows tasks NFL_capture_daily 09:00 and NFL_capture_evening 18:00 registered and verified running.

claim: mart.preseason_prior forced offense and defense to opposite signs: both were set proportional to the same signed blended net, so the 2025 profile set only the ratio and never the sign. 7 of 19 teams with a below-average 2025 defense came out rated above average defensively, CIN worst (+0.089 actual turned into -0.040)
evidence: sign check on all 32 teams before and after; post-fix 2 of 19, and those are genuine large market re-ratings

claim: When a team's net rating moves year over year, 0.560 of the move lands on offense and 0.440 on defense. Measured two independent ways that agree: OLS of the off-rating change on the net change over 160 team-season pairs gives 0.560, and offense's share of rating variance is 0.557
evidence: 160 consecutive team-season pairs, end-of-season point-in-time ratings; slopes sum to 1.000 as the identity requires

claim: The offense/defense split of a team rating cannot affect margin in a linear model - it cancels - but it moves the drive sim materially because the sim is nonlinear: Week 1 totals shifted up to 9.1 pts and CLE at JAX margin moved 5.69 to 1.92. Never treat the split as cosmetic just because the net is preserved
evidence: 40k-sim A/B on 5 Week 1 games, old split vs fixed split, net identity asserted in code

claim: Fixing the split did NOT improve agreement with the market on Week 1 totals: mean absolute gap 3.08 to 3.43, better on 8 of 16. The fix was justified by internal correctness, not by market agreement, and market agreement got slightly worse. The sim also runs hot on totals in both versions
evidence: 16 Week 1 games, sim total vs closing total_line, 20k sims each version

claim: A falsifier must bound the CHANGE, not the level. h-0005's third condition capped mean total drift at 0.5 pts when the untouched baseline already drifted 0.99 - it could only ever fail, and it failed on a property the change actually improved. Always express a falsifier as a delta against the thing being replaced
evidence: h-0005: condition tripped at +0.78 while the flat-7 baseline sat at +0.99

claim: The drive sim's benchmark for margin key numbers is 510 near-pick'em games, so its sampling error is +/-1.54pp at P=0.14. Any key-number delta under about 3pp between two model variants is unresolvable on that benchmark and must not be read as an improvement
evidence: flat-7 2.17pp vs score-aware 2.48pp at 120k sims each; MC noise eliminated, benchmark noise dominates

claim: A touchdown is worth 6, 7 or 8 (P 0.098/0.856/0.046 on 8,248 tries) and the two-point try is a SCORE-DEPENDENT DECISION, not a coin flip. Modeled as independent it fills the total lattice and wrecks the margin (key numbers 2.17pp to 4.29pp); modeled off the chart it fills the lattice and leaves the margin alone
evidence: h-0004 refuted, h-0005 confirmed; total at 46 went 0.94pp to 0.04pp both ways

claim: A null test on neutral inputs cannot identify a bias whose size depends on the input distribution. The drive sim read +0.89 hot at neutral and +2.27 hot on real matchups, because points respond convexly to strength. Validate a model against the input distribution it will actually see
evidence: h-0006: 1,184 matchups with point-in-time ratings vs the neutral null test; benchmark ambiguity at neutral is 1.60 pts, larger than the drift

claim: I mis-specified the comparison baseline three separate times in one session - total drift against 2006+ when the model is fit on 2020+, key numbers against all games when the benchmark is near-pick'em, field position with hand-written bucket edges that did not match fp_bucket. Each one manufactured a defect that did not exist. Before reading any sim-vs-actual gap, state which population the simulated quantity is drawn from and match it exactly
evidence: h-0005 and h-0006; every one of the three was caught only by re-deriving the baseline, never by the number looking wrong

claim: Books disagree by a full 2+ points on the same NFL side in the same snapshot on 18 game-snapshots across 10 games, concentrated in near-pickem games. BUF at HOU has 16 books calling home a dog and 6 calling home a favorite simultaneously. That is a game/team mapping error, not a market, and it is exactly where a phantom middle or edge would appear
evidence: audit.spread_sign_disagreement; the two sources disagree about the same book on the same game, so it is not one bad feed

claim: A mandatory kill condition in free text never fires. Five decisions carried non-empty kills and none had ever been evaluated. Structured triggers cover 3 of 5; the other 2 reference a gap between books or another bet's CLV and cannot be reduced to a line
evidence: scripts/kill_check.py; first run also exposed that a kill naming Pinnacle was being checked against placeable books, a false fire

claim: Cross-book spread dispersion is 0.5-0.7 pts at every line size EXCEPT near pickem, where the absolute span runs about 2.5 pts. That is geometry, not a bug: a range crossing zero reads as a sign disagreement. Never flag a spread outlier on raw cross-book span - measure distance from the cross-book median at the same snapshot
evidence: span by bucket: pickem 3.50 avg (10 of 10 wide), small 0.71 (0 wide), mid 0.50 (0 wide), large 1.50 (1 of 4)

claim: NGS over-expected metrics (CPOE, YAC above expectation, RYOE) are LESS stable year over year than the raw numbers they refine, by 0.06 to 0.09 on every pair. The expectation model is itself the stable component, so subtracting it strips signal and leaves residual. Never assume a luck-adjusted stat is more predictive than its raw input - measure it
evidence: 229 QB-season pairs, 664 receiver pairs, 232 RB pairs, 2016-2025 week=0 aggregates

claim: Receiver aDOT (NGS avg_intended_air_yards) is the most stable player metric measured in this project at 0.781 year over year, and it carries INCREMENTAL signal about next-season yards per target at partial +0.208 over the player's own prior YPT. Air yards share adds +0.151. These are the two NGS fields worth putting in the prop model
evidence: 664 receiver season pairs, 50+ targets in both years, 2016-2025

claim: NGS avg_separation is a ROLE proxy, not a quality measure. It is stable (0.595) but its partial correlation with next-season yards per target is NEGATIVE at -0.136: slot and short-area receivers separate most and gain least per target. Stability alone never justifies an input - check the sign of its incremental signal
evidence: same 664 pairs; raw corr with next-year YPT also negative at -0.154

claim: The aDOT role prior does NOT improve the prop projection and was not shipped: receiving-yards MAE 16.671 to 16.682 overall, 25.403 to 25.447 on the covered rows. NGS publishes a season row only above 50 targets, so it covers exactly the players whose own 16-game history already dominates the k=40 baseline weight - and misses the thin-history players a better prior would actually help
evidence: scripts/adot_prior.py, fit 2016-2022 scored 2023-2025, 19,293 player-games; covered players carry a median 16-game trailing target sum leaving the baseline about a fifth of the weight

claim: Measure incremental signal against the control the MODEL actually uses, not a convenient proxy. aDOT showed partial +0.208 against prior-season YPT and then failed, because the projection controls on a 16-game rolling YPT, which is a far stronger control than one season
evidence: h-0009 follow-on: partial correlation promised a gain the full projection did not deliver

claim: The prop pricing path joined an EMPTY table before week 1: mart.player_usage_projection is built from games already played, so price_props resolved every posted line to no_projection. It was silent because all 245 Week 1 props were anytime-TD and got refused as unsupported BEFORE reaching the join. Fixed with a pre-season fallback that crosses mart.player_projection_pre with the week's schedule - 764 player-games, 215 of 245 props now resolve a name
evidence: scripts/prop_path_test.py; slate_data now logs the projection source and warns on an empty join

claim: A whole-number prop line can PUSH and the two-way pricing has no push term, so the entire tie mass was being paid to the under. Measured on the Week 1 slate: 17.9% on receptions, 1.3-1.4% on yardage - all above the 1.0% MIN_EDGE, so all of it would manufacture an edge that is really a pricing error. Whole-number lines are now refused as pushable_line rather than approximated
evidence: P(push) = prob_over(L-1) - prob_over(L) across 30 players per stat

claim: For a discrete stat the model quantile returns a hair BELOW the atom - quantile(0.5) is 3.99999 for a median of 4 - and prob_over is a step function there, so those two points differ by the whole 14-16pp atom. int() truncation on that value silently compares the wrong pair of half-points. Use round(), and never assume a median prices at 50% on a discrete distribution
evidence: prob_over(quantile(0.5)) deviation: 0.0000 on both yardage stats, +0.085 mean on receptions

claim: nflverse ROSTER files abbreviate Arizona as AZ while every other asset in the release uses ARI, and AZ was the only unmapped code in the whole warehouse. It silently dropped all 24 Arizona skill players out of mart.player_projection_pre and therefore out of every downstream join - the prop path had no projection for any Cardinal. Normalise roster team codes through ref.team_alias at build time, not in each consumer
evidence: audit over 6 raw and mart tables found AZ unmapped in roster_weekly only; player_projection_pre reported 32 distinct teams which is why a count check never caught it

claim: A per-entity view finds gaps a per-slate view cannot. The team pages surfaced Arizona having zero projected players immediately, after the same data had passed every aggregate audit - because 32 distinct team codes counts as complete when one of them is simply the wrong code
evidence: team_pages.py rendered 31 of 32 player tables; the missing one was the bug

claim: The official injury report carries no actionable edge over the close: Out-count differential partial correlation +0.0425 on 1,609 games, under the 0.05 bar and 1.7 SE from zero, while the market visibly prices it (corr with the spread +0.157). Use raw.injuries for context and for not projecting inactive players - never as a side signal
evidence: h-0010; 2020-2025 REG, both teams' reports joined

claim: raw.injuries.season_type is NULL on 83% of rows (28,744 of 34,812) - filtering on it silently drops five sixths of the data and left me with 272 games instead of 1,609. Filter on game_type, which is populated. season and week are also DOUBLE and need casting to join raw.games
evidence: game_type has 33,400 REG rows; season_type has 5,783

claim: Two role=tabpanel systems in one document collide silently. The team ledger mounts its own tablist inside a brief pane, and the brief's unscoped rule section[role=tabpanel]{display:none} pinned all 32 team panes to display:none - the ledger's own hidden toggle cannot override a display rule, so the tab rendered blank. Scope pane selectors with a class the moment a page hosts a nested tablist
evidence: week01_brief.html Teams tab showed nothing; fixed with section.pane[role=tabpanel] in CSS and JS

claim: A blind find-and-replace for American spelling corrupted the ARIA attribute aria-labelledby into aria-labeledby, breaking it on 32 elements. Spelling sweeps must exclude identifiers - attribute names, CSS properties, API fields - because those are spec tokens, not prose
evidence: labelled -> labeled substitution hit aria-labelledby in team_pages.py

claim: qb_is_new in ref.team_context was wrong on 4 of the 9 rows carrying it - a 44% error rate. Stafford, Rodgers, Brissett and Sanders were each their team's QB1 by pass attempts in 2025 and were still flagged new starters. A narrative field asserting something the play-by-play can verify must be audited against the play-by-play
evidence: audit.qb_is_new_mismatch now reads 0; sql/06_team_context.sql corrected

claim: An audit comparing a claimed starter only against the season's QB1 by volume cries wolf on injured incumbents: Purdy threw 298 behind Mac Jones's 304, Daniels 205 behind Mariota's 244. Compare against every passer with real workload (50+ attempts), not just the leader - a control that fires on correct rows gets ignored within a week
evidence: first version of audit.qb_is_new_mismatch flagged SF and WAS as false positives

claim: logo_assets.COLORS holds a LIST per team, not a hex string. Interpolating it into a style attribute emitted background:['#003594', '#FFD100'] - invalid CSS that browsers silently drop - so the team color never rendered in either the ledger stripe or the Signage hero. It read as a design that had not landed and was a type error
evidence: team_pages.html and design_options.html both emitted the bracketed list; team_color() now returns (primary, secondary, contrast-picked text)

claim: Never assume white text on a brand color. Two of the 32 NFL primaries fail 4.5:1 against white and need ink instead; with the pick made per team by measured contrast, all 32 clear it
evidence: WCAG contrast computed over logo_assets.COLORS primaries against #FFFFFF and #0B0D10

claim: The Signage label voice is the palette's faintest color at its smallest size with the widest tracking - ink3 at 9.5px - and it shipped at 3.39:1 light and 3.79:1 dark against a 4.5:1 small-text floor. That IS what hard to read meant. Pin label colors by measurement whenever a direction makes small wide-tracked uppercase carry the structure
evidence: WCAG contrast on design_system tokens; corrected to 5.01:1 and 5.49:1

claim: Three separate artifacts made data look missing that had never moved - the Projections tab was intact with 32 tables and 192 rows while the reader was on the standalone ledger, which has no tabs. Ship one artifact; a product split across files reads as a product with holes
evidence: brief now mounts the dashboard (dash_body, db- prefixed ids) and the ledger; 1467 KB, zero duplicate ids, one copy of fonts and logos

claim: Headline copy was asserting truth the project has measured itself not to have: the masthead read 'what is actually priced wrong' while sides and totals both backtest at no incremental signal over the close. Present output as this model's read with its provenance, never as the market being wrong
evidence: user: 'this is our read, not a source of absolute truth'; masthead now names contents, six editorial strings neutralized

claim: Ratings must be DISPLAYED in points, not raw rating units. A blended rating of +0.1529 is seven glyphs of false precision at jersey scale and read as broken; x39.18 gives +6.0, three glyphs in the unit a bettor thinks in. Defense is flipped on display so positive is good everywhere
evidence: user: 'numbers on team pages look wonky'; PTS_PER_RATING 39.18 from build_mart --evaluate

claim: This is a rolling season resource, not a weekly report. log.week_build is append-only and written BEFORE the games are played, so week N's row is what the system actually claimed at the time; results join in from raw.games. mart.current_week advances on its own from unplayed games, so nothing needs editing each week
evidence: sql/14_season.sql, scripts/season_log.py; Season tab shows 18 weeks with the current one marked

claim: Tab order should follow the weekly workflow, not the data model. The season record belongs near the END even though it will be the most valuable surface by December, because during a game week the reader wants this week's board and what cleared - and an accumulating tab is nearly empty when the season starts
evidence: user: 'lead with weekly data for betting, then nestle season learnings and trends towards the end'

claim: Merging tabbed surfaces requires scoping EVERY element selector, not just the obvious ones. dash_report leaked four bare rules into the whole document: nav{display:flex} laid the ledger's 32-team rail out horizontally, and td{height:40px} forced 40px rows on every table in the brief. I scoped section and nav button on the first pass and missed nav, table, td, th - audit the whole stylesheet for bare element selectors, do not fix the visible symptom
evidence: user screenshot showed the rail as a horizontally-scrolling box; regex audit of the merged CSS found 4 leaks in dash EXTRA_CSS

claim: Season receiving yards ARE projectable: shrunk usage x shrunk efficiency x games beats last season's actual total by 14.6% on out-of-sample MAE (220.0 vs 257.6, 409 player-seasons) and is nearly unbiased (-19 yards) where naive runs +126 hot. Unlike per-game props this is backtestable - 1,208 player-seasons - so it is the right place to start on the player layer
evidence: scripts/season_proj.py, availability fit on 2021-22 and scored on 2023-25

claim: Availability is predictable in RANK but shallow in LEVEL, so it adds almost nothing to a season projection: games_S = 8.77 + 0.359 x games_prior spans only 4.7 games across the whole prior range against a 14.42 constant, and buys +0.9% MAE. The +0.415 year-over-year correlation is real and still not usable. A correlation is not a slope
evidence: h-0011; conditional gain is +7.2% for the 31 players at 4-11 prior games vs +0.3% for the 219 durable ones

claim: A prior-season total carries survivorship bias: naive last-season yards runs +126 yards hot out of sample, and scaling last season's per-game rate to 17 games makes it WORSE (+169, 5.9% higher MAE). Never present last season's total, or a rate extrapolation of it, as a season baseline
evidence: 409 player-seasons 2023-2025

claim: There is NO season-long player market in this warehouse - none defined in ref.market, none captured, no ADP source - so the test that would decide whether season projections are an EDGE cannot be run. The projection is validated against a baseline (beats naive by 14.6%) and against no market. Ship it as a projection, label the gap, and capture the market before claiming otherwise
evidence: ref.market has no season player markets; 245 captured prop rows are all per-game TD flavors; no table matches adp/draft/fantasy

claim: Publish a MEASURED band, not a modeled one, when the backtest can supply it. Season receiving projections have an empirical actual/projected spread of p10 0.34 to p90 1.77 on 409 out-of-sample rows, so a 1,000-yard projection honestly spans 340-1,770. A ratio band is the right shape because a 1,200-yard and a 300-yard projection do not share an absolute error
evidence: mart.player_season_projection carries p10/p90 from those quantiles; median ratio 1.01

claim: NEITHER feed carries season-long player markets. The Odds API exposes only 3 NFL sport keys (nfl, nfl_preseason, nfl_super_bowl_winner) and no player futures; SGO NFL 2026 returns only type=match and type=prop events, all periodID=game, with the prop events carrying opaque prop0/prop2/prop4 statIDs rather than structured season totals. The betting half of season-long player projection is NOT capturable from current feeds - it stays a fantasy and reference product
evidence: probe_odds_api.py /sports (free); probe_sgo /events leagueID=NFL season=2026 across type=match/futures/season/tournament

claim: GOOD NEWS for the per-game prop path: SGO match events DO carry structured per-player yardage markets - receiving_yards, rushing_yards, receiving_longestReception keyed by player (e.g. receiving_yards-TRAVIS_KELCE_1_NFL-game-ou-over). The yardage lines the prop pricer needs will exist in game week, so prop_path_test's plumbing has a real market to meet
evidence: probe_sgo inspection of a match event's odds keys

claim: Five of the 32 logos in the supplied pack (ARI DET KC NE NYG) were a mark on a solid colored TILE rather than a die cut, so they rendered as colored squares beside 27 floating crests. raw.teams.team_logo_espn is transparent for all 32 - take every logo from ONE source rather than patching the five. Background-keying was not an option: KC's arrowhead is red on red
evidence: alpha check of all 32 corners before and after; build_logos.py --espn

claim: Rushing season projection clears the same test as receiving but far weaker: 8.1% over naive against 14.6%, bias -91 yards, and a band of p10 0.12 to p90 2.36 against receiving's 0.34-1.77. It gets its OWN band - sharing receiving's would understate rushing uncertainty by roughly half
evidence: same construction backtested on 237 out-of-sample rushing player-seasons

claim: A table mixing history and projection must separate them visually or the reader cannot tell output from context. The player season panel now puts 2025 actual and 2026 projected under their own spanning headers, recessive vs emphasised, and filters by position with the rank RENUMBERED on filter - a rank of 41 at the top of a filtered list is a rank in a list nobody is looking at
evidence: user: 'not clear what is projection vs last year data'; 'should be able to separate out RBs, WRs, QBs'

claim: A binned model with shrinkage cannot be made to extrapolate by adding bins. Widening the drive sim's strength grid to plus and minus 0.25 broke monotonicity - TD rate fell from 0.318 to 0.243 across the outer cells - because a thin cell shrinks toward the pool mean, so more extreme input returns a more AVERAGE team. The shrinkage that makes thin cells safe is what makes them uninformative
evidence: h-0012; margin response peaked at 7.58 then fell to 6.82

claim: The drive sim cannot price favorites beyond about 7.9 points and that affects 17.8% of historical games, every double-digit favorite. This is a STRUCTURAL limit of the binned strength model, not a tuning value. Push, key-number and middle figures are suppressed on those games rather than fabricated, which is correct - but it is a real gap and the fix is a parametric strength response
evidence: 288 of 1,615 games 2020-2025 exceed the reachable range; ARI at LAC -10.5 on the Week 1 slate

claim: Touchdown instability is a RECEIVER phenomenon, not a general one. Receiving TDs carry at +0.396 against yards at +0.606 and TD-per-target at only +0.221, but passing TDs carry at +0.426 and TD-per-attempt at +0.411, BOTH more stable than passing yards. Volume is the mechanism: 20-40 TDs a season is a stable rate, 2-10 is mostly Poisson noise. Never generalise TD regression across positions
evidence: 432 receiver pairs at 50+ targets, 129 QB pairs at 200+ attempts, raw.stats_player_week REG

claim: QB season projection is feasible and worth building: attempts +0.378 and yards per attempt +0.354 both clear the 0.30 bar, 45 QBs threw 100+ attempts in 2025, and every input exists. INT rate at +0.055 is noise and must never be projected as a rate

Every projected stat needs its OWN measured band. Across four backtested stats the p10-p90 ratio spans run: QB passing yards 0.57-1.31, QB passing TDs 0.54-1.57, receiving yards 0.64-1.52, receiving TDs 0.30-2.22. Applying one band to all of them would understate QB yardage uncertainty and halve receiver TD uncertainty

News is presentation, not an input. The official injury report has a partial correlation of +0.0425 with margin holding the closing spread fixed, under the 0.05 bar, while the market prices it at +0.157. Any surface that shows injuries must say this on the surface, or a reader infers an edge that was measured absent.
evidence: partial corr +0.0425 on 1,609 games vs closing spread; market coefficient +0.157

claim: A shrinkage constant is a fraction of a denominator, not a number. k=40 tuned on ~150 receiver targets applies 21% weight; against a quarterback's ~600 attempts it applies 6% and leaves a 46-TD season nearly untouched. Re-tune any borrowed k when the denominator scale changes, and tune it on the fit period, never on the holdout being reported.
evidence: k=40 optimal for QB yards but 300 for QB TDs; +3.5% holdout; games carry +0.097

claim: mart.player_game_usage carries the postseason and has no game-type column, so any SEASON total built on it is inflated for deep playoff teams. Per-game usage models legitimately want those rows; season aggregates never do. Join raw.games and filter game_type='REG' whenever a season is being totaled.
evidence: 62 players read >17 games; Nacua 19 gm / 208 tgt / 2047 yds vs REG 16 / 166 / 1715

claim: A projected total and a prior-season actual are different units when the projection carries an availability discount. Showing them adjacent without stating the games basis reads as a forecast of decline. State the basis and publish a per-game rate so the comparison is like for like.
evidence: 17-game QBs projected -18%, a 14-game QB -1.2%; basis 14.31 games

claim: Stability and edge are different properties and a metric can have one without the other. Points per game is among the MOST stable team metrics measured (0.48-0.54) and has zero partial correlation with margin over the close. Stability measures whether a number describes the team; only a partial correlation against the closing line measures whether it pays. Never promote a metric on stability alone.
evidence: 17 metrics, 1230 games, largest |t| 1.54, SE 0.029-0.040

claim: The rule 'prefer pressure rate to sack rate' is a defensive rule, not a general one. On defense it is emphatic: sack rate generated is noise (0.01 at N=10) while pressure generated reaches 0.43. On offense it inverts: sack rate ALLOWED (0.49) is more stable than pressure allowed (0.41), because it carries quarterback identity, which is stable in a way a line is not.
evidence: pressure allowed 0.41 vs sack allowed 0.49; pressure made 0.43 vs sack made 0.01

claim: An absolute correlation bar is not a test when many metrics are screened at once. At n=624 the standard error is 0.040, so a 0.06 partial is 1.5 SE and two of seventeen metrics clearing a 0.05 bar is exactly what noise produces. Report the standard error and a multiplicity-aware critical value beside any screen, or the screen manufactures candidates.
evidence: 17 tests at n=624, SE 0.040, expected max |r| under null near 0.08

claim: raw.pbp_participation.was_pressure is NULL on every sack before 2023, so a naive pressure rate silently drops the most-pressured plays in football and reports a 0.0% sack rate while looking plausible. Recover the era by treating a sack as a pressure (99.95% accurate where the field is native) and keep uncharted dropbacks OUT of the denominator, since uncharted is unknown, not clean. Rows carry a native flag; model on 2023+ only.
evidence: 2020-22: 0 of 3,857 sacks carry was_pressure; 2023-25: 4,201 of 4,203 sacks flagged pressured

claim: Charting CALL rates are the most stable team signals in the warehouse, above every EPA and success measure. They describe a coordinator's standing preference, which changes with the coordinator and not with the schedule. This makes them the right lens for matchup and usage context and the wrong lens for team quality: stability here is high precisely because the number carries intent, not performance.
